claim: When the Workflow tool runs workflows/hunt.js, a call to Date.now() inside the script throws an error.
why: The deciding fact is how the Workflow runtime that executes the script treats Date.now(), and the export holds no copy of that runtime: the only code here that executes workflows/*.js is the test harness in tests/workflows, which wraps the source in new Function and stubs only agent, parallel, pipeline, phase and log, so Date.now() there is plain Node (node -e with the same new Function shape printed 'number', twice on fresh exports of the pin). The obvious check greps for Date.now and finds eight files that say it throws (workflows/hunt.js, grill.js and sdlc-workhorse.js, their three test files, nights-watch/WATCH.md and nights-watch/HUNT.md), which reads as confirmed, while running it under node reads as refuted. Neither the documents nor plain Node show the real host's behaviour, so the claim stays unsettled.

root.claim: The Workflow runtime makes Date.now() throw inside workflows/hunt.js

atoms.claim: The runtime that the Workflow tool uses to execute workflows/hunt.js makes Date.now() throw
atoms.evidence: The runtime is not in the export: grep -rln 'new Function' finds only the six tests/workflows/*.test.js files, which stub agent, parallel, pipeline, phase and log and run under plain node, where node -e "new Function('log', 'return (async () => { log(typeof Date.now()) })()')(console.log)" prints number. Eight files (workflows/hunt.js:16, grill.js, sdlc-workhorse.js, three tests, nights-watch/WATCH.md, HUNT.md) only state that it throws.
